## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cakkavākajātaka* (Ja 451) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887]. In the frame story (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha relates the discourse at Jetavana regarding a greedy monk (*lolabhikkhu*) who neglected his monastic duties to constantly inquire after food invitations and meat [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887]. To show that this monk's excessive craving had caused him hardship in the past, the Buddha recounts the story of the past (*atītavatthu*) [SuttaCentral]. 

In the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a ruddy goose or red-duck (*cakkavāka*) dwelling with his mate along the Ganges [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1887]. A greedy crow, noticing the duck's radiant and well-conditioned form, inquires with the opening verse beginning *Vaṇṇavā abhirūpo si* ("Fine-coloured art thou"), assuming the duck achieves beauty by gorging on river fish [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887]. The Bodhisatta explains that his beauty and happiness do not arise from slaughter or meat, but from harmlessness, virtue, and contented living [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1887]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the crow is identified with the greedy monk, the female duck with Rāhula's mother, and the ruddy duck with the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1887].

SuttaCentral records resembling parallels concerning loving-kindness and harmlessness in the *Mettāsutta* (AN 8.1), the *Mettābhāvanā Sutta* (Iti 27), and a Chinese translation (T 765.50 修慈), as well as an explicit mention of the narrative in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.11, *Ahiṁsāniggahapañha*) [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analyses, DharmaNexus records 6 matches with the commentary in the fourth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as cross-language verse alignments with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* of Subaši [DharmaNexus].
